title: Developing W/ Flexibility | Master Class | Chess Speedrun | Grandmaster Naroditsky

moves.spoken: We're White, hoping for another Danish — d4, e5, e4, building a broad center.
Black plays the knight to c6, declining the gambit. It's fine, not a terrible move.
We want to open the center as much as possible — the more open it is, the more chances to attack — so we take, d takes e5.
Black recaptures, the knight to e5. Some of you are eyeing f4, but that knight is genuinely well centralized, so let's develop first.
The knight to c3 — developing flexibly and keeping our options open.
Black plays d6 — and that's what flexible development gets you: we waited, and now he's shown us he'll castle short.
Once Black castles short, we'll have carte blanche to storm our pawns. The bishop to e3.
The bishop to g4 is a common slight mistake — it lets us shore up the e4-pawn.
f3 — a move I know causes confusion, because didn't I just warn that pushing the f-pawn creates weakness?
But things have changed: because we're about to castle long, f3 turns from a liability into a huge asset, covering e4 and building the chain. Black plays the bishop to h5.
The queen to d2, connecting the plan and preparing to castle queenside.
Black plays c5 without developing a piece — and now the d5-square becomes a very juicy outpost for us.
We castle long — now it's easy to operate, because we don't have to worry about our own king.
Black develops the knight to f6.
By the book we'd hold off, but let's go — g4, offering the pawn and prying open lines.
Black takes on g4 with the bishop.
We recapture with the f-pawn, Black takes back with the knight — and now, and only now, we've won a piece.
Time to develop the bishop with tempo — the bishop to b5 with check.
If Black knew what was good he'd block with the knight, but instead he plays the king to e7 — and this is going to get juicy.
The knight to d5 with check, driving the king forward.
Black plays the king to e6, marching into the open — exactly where a lot of players get confused.
The right piece for a hunt like this is a screwdriver piece, a knight that can wiggle in around the edges — the knight to h3, and Black grabs on e3.
And that knight arrives on f4 — checkmate.
